::: {.callout-note}
## What you will do

Starting from the converged `pitzDaily` case of the
[OpenFOAM how-to](../openfoam/how-to.qmd), you will run a **controlled parameter
study**: change *one* numerical ingredient at a time — the **mesh** and the
**discretization scheme** — and measure how the solution responds. This is
exactly how a practising CFD engineer builds trust in a result.

Two skills run through the whole assignment:

1. a reusable **Python measure** — the **reattachment length** behind the step —
   that turns each run into a single number you can compare (Task 1);
2. **research data management (RDM)**: organising your cases so that *you in six
   months*, or a collaborator, can tell at a glance what each run was and
   reproduce it.

We keep the turbulence model fixed at $k$–$\varepsilon$ throughout; comparing
turbulence models ($k$–$\omega$ SST and others) comes in a later assignment.

**You do *not* submit the cases themselves.** Instead you submit a **screenshot of
your folder structure**, your **README**, your **script names**, and a few key
plots — see [What to submit](#what-to-submit).
:::

## Research data management {#sec-rdm}

A simulation you cannot find, explain, or rerun in a year is worth very little —
and "a year" often turns out to be "next week". Good data management makes your
work **findable, accessible, interoperable and reusable** (the *FAIR* principles [@wilkinson2016]):
it is what separates a result you can defend in your thesis from a folder of
`test`, `test2`, `test_final` nobody can decode. Get into the habit now, on a
five-case study, so it is automatic when you have five hundred.

For this assignment, follow three rules:

- **Number every folder and standalone script** with a three-digit, zero-padded
  prefix, in steps of ten (`000_`, `010_`, `020_`, …) so they sort in run order and
  you can slot a new one in between later. Name each after the *one thing* it is —
  the case's single change, or what the script does. The one exception: files that
  live *inside* an importable Python package are **not** prefixed, because a leading
  digit is not a valid module name — the package name carries the ordering instead.
- **Write a README** at the top of the study that says who/what/when, the software
  and version, what each case varies, how to reproduce it, and the headline result.
- **Keep post-processing in numbered scripts**, not in your shell history — a
  committed script *is* the reproducibility.

A structure that satisfies all three:

```text
2b_backward_step/
├── README.md                   # the map to everything below
├── 000_baseline/               # reference: baseline mesh, linearUpwind
├── 010_mesh_fine/              # Study A: refined mesh, everything else identical
├── 020_scheme_upwind/          # Study B: 1st-order upwind
├── 030_scheme_linear/          # Study B: central (linear)
└── 900_postproc/               # analysis, kept apart from the run data
    └── 010_reattachment.py     # Task 1 — one script, run on every case
```

A minimal `README.md` (Markdown, so it renders anywhere):

```markdown
# Assignment 2b — backward-facing step parameter study
Author: <name> · Date: 2026-10 · Solver: simpleFoam (OpenFOAM v2412)

Quantity of interest: reattachment length x_r behind the step (see 900_postproc/).

| case               | changed vs. baseline        | x_r / h |
|--------------------|-----------------------------|:-------:|
| 000_baseline       | —                           |         |
| 010_mesh_fine      | ~2x cells in blockMeshDict  |         |
| 020_scheme_upwind  | div(phi,U) = upwind         |         |
| 030_scheme_linear  | div(phi,U) = linear         |         |

Reproduce: in each case run `blockMesh && simpleFoam`, then
`python 900_postproc/010_reattachment.py <case>`.
```

## Baseline

Create the study folder following the structure above, copy a **fresh**
`pitzDaily` from the OpenFOAM tutorials in as `000_baseline`, and run it once ---
this converged baseline is the reference every other run is compared against:

```bash
module load openfoam/v2412
cd /scratch/$USER
mkdir -p 2b_backward_step/900_postproc && cd 2b_backward_step
cp -r $FOAM_TUTORIALS/incompressible/simpleFoam/pitzDaily 000_baseline
cd 000_baseline && blockMesh && simpleFoam && cd ..
```

::: {.callout-note}
The fresh `pitzDaily` writes **streamlines** but no residuals. For the
residual-convergence plot (submission item 4), add the `solverInfo` function object
to `000_baseline/system/controlDict` **before** running --- see *Function objects*
in the [OpenFOAM how-to](../openfoam/how-to.qmd) --- then `simpleFoam` again.
:::

Start the `README.md` now and fill the results table as you go — not the night
before the deadline.

## Task 1 — Find the reattachment point

Behind the step the flow separates and rolls up into a recirculation bubble, then
**reattaches** to the lower wall further downstream. The distance from the step to
that point, the **reattachment length** $x_r$, is *the* classic scalar for this
flow — one number that summarises the whole recirculation and reacts sharply to
mesh and scheme. You will compute it in Python and reuse it for every case.

Formally, reattachment is where the **wall shear stress changes sign**
($\tau_w=0$). A robust, mesh-friendly surrogate is the **near-wall streamwise
velocity**: just above the lower wall $U_x<0$ inside the recirculation (backflow)
and $U_x>0$ once the flow has reattached, so $x_r$ is the first sign change.

Sample $U$ along a horizontal line one or two cells above the lower wall. Create a
sampling function object `system/singleGraph` (read the exact wall $y$ off
ParaView --- the numbers here are illustrative for `pitzDaily`):

```{.cpp filename="system/singleGraph"}
type                sets;
libs                (sampling);
setFormat           raw;
interpolationScheme cellPoint;
fields              (U);

sets
{
    line
    {
        type    uniform;
        axis    x;                     // first column of the .xy file is x
        start   (0      -0.0250 0);    // at the step, ~1 cell above the wall
        end     (0.29   -0.0250 0);    // to the outlet
        nPoints 200;
    }
}
```

Then sample the converged field --- this writes
`postProcessing/singleGraph/<time>/line_U.xy`:

```bash
cd 000_baseline
postProcess -func singleGraph -latestTime
```

Then find the zero crossing in `900_postproc/010_reattachment.py`:

::: {#c4434108 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.python .cell-code}
import numpy as np, glob, os, sys

case = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "000_baseline"

# find the sampled line, whatever the exact time-dir / file name is
hits = sorted(glob.glob(f"{case}/postProcessing/**/*.xy", recursive=True))
if not hits:
    raise SystemExit(
        f"No sampled .xy under {case}/postProcessing/ (cwd = {os.getcwd()}).\n"
        f"Run  `postProcess -func singleGraph -latestTime`  inside {case} first, and\n"
        f"launch this from the folder that *contains* {case}.\n"
        f"See what was written with:  ls -R {case}/postProcessing")
xy = hits[-1]
print("reading:", xy)

d      = np.loadtxt(xy)
x, Ux  = d[:, 0], d[:, 1]         # axis x -> columns: x, Ux, Uy, Uz

# reattachment: first place the near-wall Ux turns from backflow (-) to forward (+)
s     = np.sign(Ux)
cross = np.where((s[:-1] < 0) & (s[1:] >= 0))[0]
if len(cross) == 0:
    raise SystemExit("No backflow->forward sign change on this line --- check the "
                     "sampling height (it may sit above the recirculation).")
i     = cross[0]
x_r   = x[i] - Ux[i] * (x[i+1] - x[i]) / (Ux[i+1] - Ux[i])   # linear interpolation

h = 0.0254                        # step height [m] — check against your blockMeshDict
print(f"{case}:  x_r = {x_r*1e3:.1f} mm = {x_r/h:.2f} h")
```
:::


::: {.callout-important}
## Task 1 — deliverable
Your `900_postproc/010_reattachment.py`, and the baseline $x_r$ (in mm and in step heights $h$).
This is the measure you report for **every** case below.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="solutions"}
::: {.solution-box}
For the coarse `pitzDaily` baseline expect $x_r$ of order a few step heights; the
exact value is mesh- and scheme-dependent (which is the point of Studies A and B).
Watch for a spurious early crossing right at the step corner (a tiny corner
vortex); take the crossing that ends the *main* recirculation. Reading $\tau_w$
from `wallShearStress` on the `lowerWall` patch is the exact method and earns
bonus credit.
:::
:::

## Study A — Mesh sensitivity

Refine the mesh and check whether your answer has stopped changing (grid
independence).

- Copy the baseline to `010_mesh_fine`. In `system/blockMeshDict`, roughly **double**
  the cell counts (the numbers in the `hex (...) (nx ny nz) ...` lines), then rerun
  `blockMesh` + `simpleFoam` and `900_postproc/010_reattachment.py`.
- Compare $x_r$ on coarse vs. fine. Does it converge?

::: {.callout-important}
## A — deliverable
$x_r$ on both meshes, and one sentence: is the baseline mesh fine enough?
:::

## Study B — Discretization scheme (numerical diffusion)

Change **only** the convection scheme for momentum in `system/fvSchemes`, in a
fresh numbered case each time, and rerun:

```cpp
div(phi,U)   bounded Gauss upwind;                 // 1st order  -> 020_scheme_upwind
div(phi,U)   bounded Gauss linearUpwind grad(U);   // 2nd order  -> 000_baseline (already have it)
div(phi,U)   Gauss linear;                          // central    -> 030_scheme_linear
```

Compare the velocity field and $x_r$ across the three. Which smears the shear
layer? Does the central scheme show any oscillations or convergence trouble?

::: {.callout-important}
## B — deliverable
One comparison plot (field or profile) of the three schemes plus their $x_r$, and
two–three sentences linking what you see to **numerical diffusion** vs.
**boundedness** from the lectures.
:::

## What to submit {#what-to-submit}

Upload to Crowdmark — **not** the cases themselves, but the evidence that you ran
and organised them well:

1. **A screenshot of your folder structure** showing the numbered cases, the
   `README.md`, and the `900_postproc/` scripts. On the cluster, `tree -L 2
   2b_backward_step` (or a file-browser screenshot) is perfect.
2. **Your `README.md`** (as text or a screenshot), with the results table filled in.
3. **Your script name(s)** — i.e. `010_reattachment.py` — visible in the tree above,
   plus the script's contents pasted once.
4. **Key plots (≤ 5).** Residual convergence for one run; a velocity-magnitude
   field; and the comparison of $x_r$ across Studies A and B.
5. **Short discussion (≤ ½ page).** Answer the deliverable questions above.

::: {.callout-tip}
Change **one thing at a time** and keep the baseline fixed — otherwise you cannot
attribute a difference to any single cause. Note the wall-clock and iteration
count for each run; refinement and higher-order schemes cost more.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="solutions"}
::: {.solution-box}
**Expected trends (instructor notes).**

- **A (mesh):** the coarse baseline is somewhat under-resolved; refining
  lengthens/settles $x_r$ as numerical (mesh) diffusion drops. $x_r$ should change
  less between fine and baseline than between baseline and a deliberately coarse
  mesh — the signature of approaching grid independence.
- **B (scheme):** first-order `upwind` adds strong numerical diffusion → the shear
  layer is smeared and $x_r$ shortened/washed out. `linearUpwind` (2nd order) is
  sharper. Pure `linear` (central) is least diffusive but may show wiggles or
  slower/failed convergence on this mesh — the accuracy-vs-boundedness trade-off
  from the lecture.

Grading: reward a clean one-variable-at-a-time design, a correct and reused
reattachment measure, disciplined RDM (numbered cases, a real README, scripted
post-processing), and physical interpretation over "prettier" plots.
:::
